["The meeting is going to be beginning at noon time.","The meeting begins at noon.","The meeting, which is one that begins, begins at noon.","The meeting begins at twelve noon exactly at that time."]
The other choices are wordy or redundant.
Choose the correct word: The cat likes to ____ in the sun.
'Lie' means to recline; 'lay' needs an object.
Choose the parallel ending: The coach told us to stretch, to drink water, and ____.
["rest is needed","to rest before the game","resting","we should rest"]
The series uses 'to' plus a verb.
Which sentence has the clearest meaning?

["Sandwiches were served to the guests who were on paper plates.","On paper plates, the guests were served to sandwiches.","She served sandwiches to the guests on paper plates.","She served the guests sandwiches on paper plates."]
The modifier 'on paper plates' sits next to 'sandwiches', so the guests are not on plates.
Several students share lockers, and the lockers belong to all of them. Which is correct?
["The students lockers were freshly painted.","The student's lockers were freshly painted.","The students' lockers were freshly painted.","The students's lockers were freshly painted."]
A plural possessive ending in s takes only an apostrophe.
Choose the word that keeps the sentence parallel: The new park is both beautiful and ____.
Choose the best transition: Marcus practiced daily. ____, he won no medals this year.
The sentence shows contrast with expectations.
Which sentence has a clear, correctly modified subject?

["Having walked to school, the rain soaked the sidewalk.","Walking to school, Ben felt the rain start to fall.","Walking to school, the rain fell on Ben's head.","Walking to school, the rain started to fall."]
The introductory phrase must describe Ben, not the rain.
Which sentence has a clear pronoun reference?
["Sara told Lily that she had left her book at home.","When Sara and Lily met, she said she'd forgotten it.","Sara told Lily she left it there.","Sara said to Lily, \"I left my book at home.\""]
The quotation removes the ambiguity about who 'she' is.
Choose the correct form: If I ____ you, I would study more.
Which sentence introduces its list with correct punctuation?

["You will: need three items, a pencil, an eraser, and a ruler.","You will need three items: a pencil, an eraser, and a ruler.","You: will need three items, a pencil, an eraser and a ruler.","You will need three items a pencil: an eraser, and a ruler."]
A colon follows a complete clause before a list.
Choose the correct pronoun: Between you and ____, the test was hard.
The object of a preposition takes the objective case.
Which sentence punctuates the appositive correctly?
["My neighbor, Mr. Kim is a pilot.","My neighbor, Mr. Kim, is a pilot.","My, neighbor Mr. Kim is a pilot.","My neighbor Mr. Kim, is a pilot."]
A nonessential appositive is set off by commas on both sides.

When a honeybee discovers a rich patch of flowers, it returns to the hive and performs a special movement called a "waggle dance." The direction and length of the dance ______ information about the location of the flowers, so other bees can fly directly to the food. Scientists who have learned to interpret these dances can predict where the bees will travel next.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
The dance lets other bees find the food, so it must communicate, or convey, information about the location.

For many years, the empty lot on Pine Street collected nothing but garbage and broken glass. Then a group of neighbors decided to ______ it into a community garden. Together they cleared the ground, built wooden planting beds, and planted tomatoes, beans, and sunflowers. Today the lot provides fresh vegetables for dozens of families every summer.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
The neighbors changed a trash-filled lot into a garden, so "transform" is the precise word.

Sea otters often wrap themselves in long strands of kelp before they fall asleep at the surface. The kelp works like an anchor, preventing the otters from ______ away on ocean currents while they rest. Some otters even hold paws with one another for the same reason, forming floating groups called rafts.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
An anchor keeps something from floating away, so the kelp keeps otters from drifting.

Many people think of deserts as empty, lifeless places. In fact, the Sonoran Desert of the southwestern United States and northern Mexico is home to about 2,000 kinds of plants. After spring rains, the ground can be covered in wildflowers, and animals such as bats, tortoises, and roadrunners find food and shelter among the cactuses.
Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?

["To argue that the Sonoran Desert receives more rain than other deserts","To challenge a common belief about deserts by describing the variety of life in one desert","To explain the process by which deserts form over time","To warn readers about the dangers of traveling in the Sonoran Desert"]
The text opens with the belief that deserts are lifeless and then lists the many plants and animals of the Sonoran Desert to show that belief is wrong.

Architect Lena Osei is known for buildings that seem to ______ the laws of gravity. Her art museum in the harbor city of Port Aria includes a gallery that extends forty feet beyond its last support column, so it appears to float above the water. People walking past often stop on the sidewalk below just to stare up at it in surprise.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
A gallery that seems to float without support appears to resist, or defy, gravity.

Many early sound films were ______ by the technology of the time. Because the bulky microphones had to stay hidden and could not move, actors were often forced to stand close to potted plants or lamps while speaking, which made scenes feel stiff. Only after crews began hanging microphones from movable poles could performers walk around freely again.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
The fixed microphones limited how actors could move, so the films were constrained by the technology.

In the hot summer of 1858, the Thames River in London gave off an overwhelming stench. The river received much of the city's untreated sewage. Lawmakers in the Houses of Parliament, which stands beside the river, hung chemical-soaked curtains over their windows to block the smell. Within weeks, they approved money for a huge network of sewers. This system, designed by engineer Joseph Bazalgette, still carries much of London's waste today.
Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?

["To explain why Parliament chose to meet beside the Thames River","To compare London's sewer system with those of other large cities","To argue that Bazalgette's sewer system is now outdated","To describe how an unpleasant event led to a major public works project"]
The text tells how the 1858 stench pushed lawmakers to fund London's sewer network.

During the 1800s, ships frequently crashed on rocky coastlines at night. Lighthouses helped, but in the darkness sailors could not always tell one lighthouse from another. To solve this problem, engineers gave each lighthouse its own distinctive pattern of light: one might flash twice every ten seconds, while another shone steadily. By observing the pattern, a captain could identify the lighthouse and calculate the ship's position.
Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

["It describes the history of a single famous lighthouse from start to finish.","It identifies a problem that sailors faced and then explains how it was solved.","It compares two kinds of lighthouses and argues that one is better.","It presents a theory about shipwrecks and then gives evidence against it."]
The text first explains that sailors could not tell lighthouses apart and then describes the flash patterns that solved this problem.

Economists studying small coffee farms in Colombia found that farmers who joined cooperatives earned steadier incomes than farmers who sold their beans on their own. The researchers caution, however, that this finding is ______: the farmers who chose to join may already have had larger plots or better connections, advantages that could explain much of the difference.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
Because other factors might explain the result, the researchers treat the finding as uncertain, or tentative.

Critics have long described novelist Mara Ellison's prose as ______. Her sentences rarely exceed a dozen words, she avoids adjectives whenever possible, and entire chapters pass without a single metaphor. Yet readers often report that this stripped-down style makes her characters' grief feel more intense, not less.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
Short sentences with few adjectives and no metaphors describe a plain, severe style, which is "austere."

Octopuses can change the color and texture of their skin in a fraction of a second. For decades, researchers assumed that this ability depended entirely on what the animals saw with their eyes. Yet octopus skin itself contains light-sensitive proteins called opsins, the same molecules that allow eyes to detect light. This discovery has led some biologists to propose that octopuses may partly sense light directly through their skin.
Which choice best describes the function of the third sentence ("Yet octopus skin . . . detect light") in the overall structure of the text?

["It summarizes the main conclusion that researchers reached decades ago.","It explains why researchers stopped studying octopus eyes.","It offers an example that supports the assumption described in the previous sentence.","It presents a finding that complicates the assumption described in the previous sentence."]
Opsins in the skin suggest the skin itself may detect light, which challenges the assumption that color change depended only on the eyes.

Text 1
Many city planners argue that adding bike lanes reduces car traffic. When cycling feels safe, they say, more residents leave their cars at home, so each new lane takes some cars off the road.

Text 2
A study of bike lanes in dozens of cities found that individual lanes, built here and there, did little to change how people traveled. Car trips dropped noticeably only in cities where lanes were linked into a connected network that let riders reach most destinations without sharing busy roads.
Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the planners' claim in Text 1?

["By suggesting that the claim holds only when lanes form a connected network","By arguing that bike lanes tend to increase car traffic","By asserting that most residents prefer roads without bike lanes","By agreeing that every new bike lane removes some cars from the road"]
Text 2 found that isolated lanes had little effect and that traffic fell only with connected networks, so it would limit the planners' claim to that case.

The following text is from a poem in which the speaker reflects on a grandmother's kitchen and the cooking traditions she left behind.
Her hands kept time the clock forgot:
the knead, the fold, the patient rise;
she measured nothing, yet she knew
the weight of flour by the skies.
Now I keep her bowl, her spoon,
her recipe in fading ink,
yet every loaf comes out too soon;
the page holds less than hands could think.
Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

["The speaker recalls a single family meal and then imagines meals that will happen in the future.","The speaker lists the steps of a recipe and then explains why each one matters.","The speaker criticizes a relative's methods and then defends the speaker's own.","The speaker describes a relative's instinctive skill and then contrasts it with the speaker's own failed efforts despite having her tools."]
The first half praises the grandmother's intuitive baking; the second half shows the speaker owning her bowl and recipe but still failing.

Text 1
Sediment cores from lakes in the Maya lowlands show that the region suffered a series of severe droughts between about 800 and 1000 CE. Because many great southern Maya cities were abandoned during these same centuries, some researchers conclude that drought was the main cause of their decline.

Text 2
The droughts were real, but they cannot be the whole story. Several cities in the drier northern lowlands, such as Chichén Itzá, grew during the same period. Drought likely combined with warfare and political breakdown, which struck some regions far harder than others.
Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the conclusion of the researchers in Text 1?

["By claiming that warfare in the region had no connection to environmental conditions","By agreeing that drought alone explains why the southern cities were abandoned","By arguing that drought may have contributed to the decline but cannot fully explain it, since some cities in drier areas thrived","By questioning whether the lake sediment cores show that any droughts occurred"]
Text 2 accepts the droughts but notes that northern cities grew despite drier conditions, so drought cannot be the sole cause.

When biologist Ana Ferreira announced that she had found a new species of tree frog, many experts doubted that the animal was truly distinct from known species. Her documentation, however, was painstaking. It included hundreds of photographs, genetic sequences from twelve specimens, and recordings of the frogs' unusual calls. In the end, this evidence ______ even her harshest critics' doubts.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
Thorough evidence would remove the critics' doubts, so "dispelled" is the logical choice.

A widespread assumption holds that households save less when credit becomes easily available. Economist Priya Nand tested this assumption by tracking the finances of 3,000 households over six years. She found that households receiving new credit cards did increase their spending during the first several months. "After about a year, however, their savings rates returned almost exactly to where they had been," Nand reports. Her results suggest that credit may primarily alter the timing of consumer spending rather than its total amount.
Which choice best describes the function of the quotation from Nand in the text as a whole?

["It shows that households saved more after receiving credit than they had before.","It qualifies the finding in the previous sentence by indicating that the effect was temporary.","It introduces the common belief that Nand set out to test.","It describes the method Nand used to choose which households to study."]
The quotation shows that the higher spending faded after a year, limiting the earlier finding.

The following text is adapted from a novel. Tomas has just returned to the coastal village where he spent his childhood.
The bakery was gone; in its place stood a shop selling telephones, its window bright with screens, and Tomas stood before it longer than he had intended. He could still smell, or believed he could, the caramelized sugar of the almond cakes his aunt had pressed into his hands every Sunday morning. A young clerk inside glanced up, smiled politely, and returned to her work, and Tomas understood that she had no reason to suspect there had ever been anything else on this particular corner.
Which choice best describes the function of the final sentence in the text as a whole?

["It suggests that Tomas intends to reopen his aunt's bakery.","It emphasizes that Tomas's memories of the place are not shared by the people there now.","It explains why the bakery was replaced by a telephone shop.","It reveals that the clerk recognizes Tomas from his childhood."]
The clerk's polite indifference makes Tomas realize the bakery lives only in his own memory.

Agnes Thorne, a nineteenth-century reformer, is often remembered as a fiery public speaker. In her private correspondence, however, she was remarkably ______. Her letters weigh opposing arguments at length and concede points to her adversaries. They rarely reach a conclusion without several careful qualifications.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
Weighing arguments carefully and qualifying conclusions shows caution, which "circumspect" captures; "laconic" contradicts the lengthy letters.

Text 1
Russian has separate basic words for light blue (goluboy) and dark blue (siniy), while English uses one word, "blue." In experiments, Russian speakers distinguished shades across that boundary faster than English speakers did. Some researchers take this as evidence that the language a person speaks shapes how that person perceives color.

Text 2
The speed advantage is real, but it vanished when Russian speakers were asked to silently repeat a string of numbers during the task, which kept them from using words. This suggests that language influences perception through the active use of words in the moment, not by permanently changing how speakers see.
Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely characterize the experimental finding described in Text 1?

["As irrelevant, because Russian and English speakers can see the same range of colors","As proof that language permanently alters the way people see colors","As the result of a flawed measurement that should be disregarded","As genuine but better explained by speakers' use of words during the task than by a lasting change in perception"]
Text 2 accepts the speed advantage but argues that it depends on using words in the moment, since it disappeared when verbal processing was blocked.

Historians once portrayed the craft guilds of medieval Europe as essentially ______ institutions. In this view, guilds existed only to shield their members from competition and keep prices high. Recent archival work complicates that picture: guild records reveal extensive charitable activity, from paying for the funerals of poor members to supporting widows and orphans.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
Institutions concerned only with protecting their own profits are self-interested, or "mercenary," a view the charity records complicate.

Chess players may look as if they are sitting still, but their bodies are working hard. During long tournaments, top players' heart rates can rise as high as those of some athletes, and they breathe faster when a game becomes tense. Some players burn so much energy thinking and worrying that they lose weight over an event that lasts several days.
Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

["Chess players should exercise before every game.","Chess is more popular than many traditional sports.","Most chess players eat less during tournaments than at home.","Playing in chess tournaments can place real physical demands on players."]
The text describes rising heart rates, faster breathing, and weight loss to show that tournament chess is physically demanding.

Students at Lakeview Middle School set up a bird feeder in the yard. Each month, they counted the birds that came to it.
Month | Birds counted
October | 42
November | 58
December | 75
January | 81
The students noted that from October to January, the number of birds ______
Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
["increased every month.","was highest in November.","decreased after December.","stayed about the same each month."]
The counts rise from 42 to 58 to 75 to 81, an increase every month.

Rain gardens are shallow patches of ground planted with flowers and grasses that can handle wet soil. When it storms, water runs off roofs and driveways into the garden instead of rushing into storm drains. The plants' roots help the water soak slowly into the ground. Because of this, a town that builds many rain gardens can expect ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

["less water to flow into its storm drains during heavy rain.","fewer flowers to grow in its public parks.","storms to happen less often than before.","its roofs and driveways to stay dry during storms."]
Rain gardens catch runoff that would otherwise go into storm drains, so less water would reach the drains.

Jun Park's short story "The Long Walk Home" follows two brothers as they walk home from school on a rainy afternoon. In the story, the narrator's younger brother, Eli, is very curious about the world around him. His curiosity often slows the brothers down.
Which quotation from the story most effectively illustrates the claim?

["\"Eli stopped at every storm drain to watch the leaves spin into the dark, asking where the water went and refusing to move until I guessed.\"","\"Eli said he was hungry and hoped Mom had made soup for dinner.\"","\"Eli pulled his hood tighter and complained that his sneakers were soaking wet.\"","\"By the time we reached our street, the rain had finally stopped.\""]
Only this quotation shows Eli asking questions about what he sees and delaying the walk because of it.

The Hadza are a group of hunter-gatherers in Tanzania. Researchers measured how much energy Hadza adults used each day. Because the Hadza walk long distances daily, the team expected them to burn far more calories than office workers in the United States and Europe. But once body size was taken into account, the Hadza burned about the same number of calories per day. The results suggest that the body may keep its total energy use within a set range, even when people are very active.
Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

["Researchers have developed a new way to measure differences in body size.","A study found that very active people used about as much daily energy as less active people, suggesting the body limits total energy use.","Office workers burn more calories than hunter-gatherers because they eat more food.","The Hadza walk longer distances each day than any other group of people."]
The text centers on the surprising finding that the active Hadza burned similar calories, and what that suggests about the body.

Scientists studied a lake in the north. They recorded its average water temperature in July. They also counted the days it was covered by ice each winter.
Decade | July temperature (°C) | Days of ice cover
1980s | 21.4 | 112
1990s | 21.9 | 104
2000s | 22.5 | 97
2010s | 23.1 | 89
The scientists claim that as the lake has grown warmer in summer, its period of winter ice cover has become shorter.
Which choice best describes data from the table that support the scientists' claim?

["In the 1990s, the July temperature was 21.9°C and there were 104 days of ice cover.","The July temperature was higher in the 2000s than in the 1990s.","The July temperature rose from 21.4°C in the 1980s to 23.1°C in the 2010s, while days of ice cover fell from 112 to 89.","The lake had the most days of ice cover in the 1980s."]
Only this choice shows both trends together: rising summer temperatures and fewer days of ice.

Some kinds of fig trees can be pollinated by only one kind of tiny wasp. That wasp, in turn, can lay its eggs only inside the flowers of the same kind of fig. Neither partner can reproduce without the other. So if one of these wasps were to disappear from a forest, the matching fig trees in that forest would most likely ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?
["be unable to produce new seeds.","begin to be pollinated by other kinds of insects.","attract a different wasp species to lay its eggs.","grow more quickly than they did before."]
Since each fig depends on a single wasp for pollination, losing the wasp would stop the fig from reproducing.

Male house finches range in color from pale yellow to deep red, and females tend to prefer redder males. The red color comes from pigments called carotenoids, which the birds cannot make themselves and must get from foods such as certain berries and seeds. Finding enough of these foods takes skill and good health. Some biologists have therefore suggested that a female who chooses a red male ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

["is choosing a male that will have yellow offspring.","is choosing a male that avoids eating berries and seeds.","may be choosing a mate that is good at finding food.","cannot tell the difference between red and yellow males."]
Red color depends on finding pigment-rich foods, which takes skill and health, so a red male is likely a good forager.

The following text is from a poem describing a small fishing harbor during the long, quiet months of winter, when the boats remain ashore.
The boats are hauled and canvas-bound,
the gulls sit hunched along the pier;
no engine breaks the frozen sound
that settles on the water here.
Yet coiled ropes still smell of tar,
and nets hang stiff with August salt,
and every hull, from keel to spar,
remembers motion it was taught.
Which quotation from the poem most effectively illustrates the claim that the speaker finds traces of summer activity in the winter harbor?
["\"and nets hang stiff with August salt,\"","\"The boats are hauled and canvas-bound,\"","\"the gulls sit hunched along the pier;\"","\"no engine breaks the frozen sound\""]
Salt left from August on the nets is a trace of summer fishing; the other lines describe only the winter stillness.

Textile artist Amara Diallo builds large wall hangings from fabric scraps she collects from tailors' shops in Dakar, Senegal. Rather than hiding the scraps' origins, she preserves their frayed edges, chalk marks, and even the tailors' penciled measurements. Diallo has said that she wants viewers to sense the many unseen hands that shaped each piece before it reached her studio, so that a single artwork becomes a record of a whole community's labor.
Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

["Diallo deliberately keeps traces of the fabrics' earlier use so that her works reflect the labor of the community that produced them.","Diallo prefers new fabric but uses scraps because they cost less.","Diallo removes all marks from her materials so viewers can focus on her designs.","Tailors in Dakar have begun creating wall hangings of their own."]
The text explains that Diallo preserves the tailors' marks to make each work a record of community labor.

Researchers surveyed adults in four regions about how they usually travel to work.
Region | Drive alone (%) | Public transit (%) | Walk or bike (%)
North | 62 | 21 | 17
South | 78 | 9 | 13
East | 48 | 37 | 15
West | 70 | 12 | 18
The researchers concluded that the region with the highest share of public transit riders also had the lowest share of people who drive alone.
Which choice best describes data from the table that support the researchers' conclusion?

["In the North, 21% of adults use public transit and 62% drive alone.","In the West, 18% of adults walk or bike, the highest share of any region.","In the East, 37% of adults use public transit, more than in any other region, and 48% drive alone, less than in any other region.","In the South, 78% of adults drive alone and 9% use public transit."]
The East has both the highest transit share (37%) and the lowest drive-alone share (48%).

Archaeologists excavating a 4,000-year-old settlement found grinding stones coated with residue from wild grasses. They found no residue from wheat or barley, although those crops were grown at other sites in the region during the same period. The settlement sat on rocky hillsides far from fertile river valleys, a location that would have made farming difficult. These findings suggest that the settlement's residents ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

["relied on gathering wild plants rather than on growing crops.","grew wheat and barley but ground them somewhere else.","traded their grinding stones to farming communities in the valleys.","had never heard of wheat or barley."]
Residue only from wild grasses, plus poor farmland, points to a diet based on gathered wild plants.

The following text is adapted from a novel. Irene, a retired schoolteacher, has reluctantly agreed to tutor her neighbor's teenage son.
Irene had expected the boy to be sullen, and for the first twenty minutes he was, answering her questions in single syllables and staring past her at the window. Then she set the workbook aside and asked what he would build if he had all the lumber in the world, and for the first time, he looked directly at her. By the end of the hour, the margins of her carefully prepared lesson plan were crowded with his sketches of towers and bridges, and she had taught nothing she had planned.
Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

["By setting aside her plan, Irene finds a way to engage a reluctant student.","The boy teaches Irene how to design towers and bridges more skillfully.","Irene decides that the boy has no interest in learning and gives up on tutoring him.","Irene regrets agreeing to tutor the boy because he remains sullen throughout the lesson."]
The boy becomes engaged only after Irene abandons the workbook and asks about his interests.

A biologist hypothesized that a coastal plant grows taller in soil containing more nitrogen. She grew the plants in four soils and recorded their average heights.
Soil nitrogen (mg/kg) | Average height (cm)
10 | 18
20 | 26
40 | 33
80 | 34
She concluded that adding nitrogen increases plant height only up to a point: ______
Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?

["plants grown with 10 mg/kg of nitrogen reached an average height of 18 centimeters.","plants grown with 80 mg/kg of nitrogen were the tallest of all the groups.","plants grew 15 centimeters taller as nitrogen rose from 10 to 40 mg/kg, but only 1 centimeter taller when it doubled again to 80 mg/kg.","plants grew 8 centimeters taller as nitrogen rose from 10 to 20 mg/kg."]
Only this choice shows large gains at lower levels followed by almost no gain at the highest level, which is the limit the conclusion describes.

Psychologists gave volunteers a list of words to learn. One group reread the list repeatedly; another group spent the same amount of time trying to recall the words without looking, then checked which ones they had missed. One week later, the second group remembered substantially more words, even though members of that group had predicted they would do worse than the rereaders. These results suggest that learners ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

["remember more when they reread material many times.","perform best when they correctly predict their own scores.","may not accurately judge which study methods work best for them.","forget most information within a week no matter how they study."]
The recall group did better despite predicting worse results, so learners misjudged the effectiveness of the methods.

Coyotes now live in many large North American cities, including Chicago and Los Angeles. Some residents worry that the animals survive mainly by raiding garbage cans and pet food bowls, a habit that could make them bold around people. Wildlife ecologist Dana Ruiz argues instead that most urban coyotes have adapted by shifting their activity to avoid humans while continuing to hunt wild prey such as rodents and rabbits.
Which finding, if true, would most directly support Ruiz's argument?

["Urban coyotes are, on average, slightly larger than coyotes in rural areas.","Coyotes living in cities produce smaller litters than those in the countryside.","Many city residents report having seen coyotes near garbage cans.","Tracking collars show urban coyotes are active mostly between midnight and dawn, and their droppings contain mainly rodent and rabbit remains."]
Nighttime activity shows avoidance of people, and the droppings show a diet of wild prey, matching both parts of Ruiz's argument.

Historians of science have often portrayed France's adoption of the metric system as a triumph of Enlightenment reason over local custom. Yet records from the decades after 1795 show that many merchants and farmers kept using older units, and in 1812 the government even permitted "usual measures" that blended metric definitions with traditional names. The system became universal in France only after 1840, when its use was made compulsory.
Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

["Historians have correctly described the metric system as being adopted quickly in France.","The metric system's eventual dominance in France depended more on government requirement than on the appeal of its logic.","The \"usual measures\" of 1812 were intended to abolish the metric system entirely.","French merchants rejected the metric system because traditional units were more accurate."]
The text shows that people resisted the system until it was made compulsory, undercutting the view that reason alone made it succeed.

Researchers compared four methods of teaching fractions. They tested students immediately after instruction and again three months later.
Method | Average score right after | Average score after 3 months
Lecture | 78 | 52
Worked examples | 74 | 61
Peer discussion | 70 | 63
Hands-on models | 81 | 58
One researcher argues that the method producing the highest immediate scores is not necessarily the one producing the most lasting learning.
Which choice best describes data from the table that support the researcher's argument?

["Lecture produced an average score of 78 right after instruction, which was higher than that of worked examples.","Worked examples produced an average score of 74 right after instruction and 61 after three months.","Every method's average score was lower after three months than right after instruction.","Hands-on models produced the highest average score right after instruction (81), but peer discussion produced the highest average score after three months (63)."]
This choice shows that the method with the top immediate score was not the method with the top delayed score.

Linguists have observed a pattern in how languages change. Languages spoken by very large populations, especially those widely learned by adults as second languages, tend to have simpler systems of word endings than languages of small, isolated communities. One explanation is that adult learners struggle to master complex endings. Over generations, their simplified usage spreads through the whole community. If this explanation is correct, then a language that ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

["has complex word endings must be difficult for children to learn as a first language.","is learned mostly by children is likely to borrow many words from other languages.","spreads rapidly among adult newcomers is likely to lose some of the complexity of its word endings over time.","is spoken by a small, isolated community should quickly simplify its word endings."]
The explanation links simplification to adult learners, so a language adopted by many adult newcomers should simplify.

Some flowers turn to follow the sun across the sky. Biologist Mei Okafor hypothesizes that in the Arctic poppy, this sun-tracking benefits the plant mainly by warming the inside of the flower, which attracts insect pollinators seeking warmth in the cold climate, rather than by increasing photosynthesis in the plant's leaves.
Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okafor's hypothesis?

["Several other Arctic flowers also turn to follow the sun.","Arctic poppy leaves carry out more photosynthesis when the flowers track the sun.","Insects visit Arctic poppies more often on cloudy days than on sunny days.","Arctic poppy flowers prevented from tracking the sun were cooler inside and received fewer insect visits, while their leaves photosynthesized at normal rates."]
This finding links sun-tracking to flower warmth and insect visits while ruling out a photosynthesis benefit, matching the hypothesis.

The giant sequoias of California's Sierra Nevada are among the largest living things on Earth. A single tree can weigh more than two million pounds. The thick, spongy bark of these trees ______ them from many forest fires, which is one reason some sequoias have lived for more than 3,000 years.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
The singular subject "bark" requires the singular verb "protects."

Every spring, the town of Millbrook holds a festival to celebrate ______ history as one of the first mill towns in the region. Visitors can tour the old stone mill, watch people spin wool by hand, and taste bread baked from flour ground on the original millstones.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
"Its" is the singular possessive pronoun that refers to the town; "it's" means "it is."

Wangari Maathai founded the Green Belt Movement in Kenya in 1977. The group encouraged women to plant trees in their ______ the following decades, members planted tens of millions of trees across the country, helping to restore forests and protect soil.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
Two complete sentences must be separated with a period; the other choices create a comma splice, a run-on, or an incomplete clause.

In July 1969, the Apollo 11 lunar module landed on the Moon. About six and a half hours later, astronaut Neil Armstrong ______ down the ladder and became the first person to walk on the lunar surface. Millions of people around the world watched the historic moment on television.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
The event happened in the past and the sentence uses "became" and "watched," so the simple past "climbed" is needed.

During the 2010s, many cities replaced their old streetlights with LED fixtures. The ______ lower energy use allowed some cities to cut their lighting costs by more than half. The brighter, whiter light also helped security cameras record clearer images at night.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
The energy use belongs to the plural "fixtures," so the plural possessive "fixtures'" is correct.

Marine biologist Rosa Linde spent three months living in an underwater research station off the coast of Florida. Each day, she watched the reef fish that gathered around its windows. She focused on one kind of fish in ______ the bluehead wrasse, a small fish that can change from female to male.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
A colon correctly introduces the phrase naming the species; the other choices create a fragment or join a clause to a non-clause.

The collection of letters, diaries, and photographs that historian Lucia Moreno discovered in an attic in Santa Fe ______ new insight into daily life in New Mexico during the 1880s. Moreno plans to post the materials online so that other researchers can study them.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
The subject is the singular "collection," not "photographs," so the singular verb "offers" is required.

The tardigrade, a microscopic animal sometimes called a "water bear," is famously hard to kill. In laboratory tests, tardigrades have survived temperatures near absolute zero, intense radiation, and even exposure to the vacuum of space. Scientists who study these tiny creatures ______ to learn how their cells resist damage, research that could someday help preserve vaccines without refrigeration.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
The subject is the plural "Scientists," not "creatures," so the plural verb "hope" is required.

When the members of the city council reviewed the proposal for a new public library, ______ were especially impressed by its plan to include a workshop with 3D printers and sewing machines. After a brief discussion, the council voted unanimously to fund the project.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
The pronoun refers to the plural "members" and must agree with the plural verb "were," so "they" is correct.

Most meteorites that land on Earth come from the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter. A small number, however, have a far stranger ______ were blasted off the surface of Mars by ancient impacts. Scientists identify them by comparing gases trapped inside the rocks with measurements of the Martian atmosphere.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
["origin, they","origin: they","origin they","origin, and that they"]
A colon correctly joins the independent clause to a second clause that explains the "stranger origin"; the others create a comma splice, a run-on, or a faulty structure.

In 1922, the poet and teacher Elena Vasquez founded a small press in her San Antonio home, ______ dozens of chapbooks by local writers over the next two decades. Many of those chapbooks, long thought lost, were recently rediscovered in the archives of a university library.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
The participle "printing" correctly introduces a modifying phrase; the other choices create a comma splice or an incorrectly joined verb.

One of the most striking findings in urban ecology is that songbirds in noisy cities often sing at higher pitches than rural birds of the same species. Biologist Hans Slabbekoorn, who first documented this pattern in great tits, ______ that the higher notes help the birds' songs rise above the low rumble of traffic.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
The subject "Hans Slabbekoorn" needs a finite main verb, and only "argues" supplies one.

A museum's new exhibit features artifacts from three ancient cities: Ur, in present-day ______ Mohenjo-daro, in present-day Pakistan; and Teotihuacan, in present-day Mexico. Curators selected these three sites because each was among the largest urban centers of its era. Together, they show how differently early cities could develop.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
Because the list items already contain commas, semicolons must separate them, matching the semicolon after "Pakistan."

Economist Elinor Ostrom spent decades studying communities that share resources such as fisheries and forests. Conventional theory predicted that such shared resources would inevitably be ______ Ostrom documented many cases in which local groups created their own rules. Some of these groups sustained their resources for centuries.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
A semicolon is needed between the two independent clauses, and "however" belongs to the second clause, followed by a comma.

Among the most impressive achievements of the Inca Empire ______ the road network known as the Qhapaq Ñan, which stretched for tens of thousands of kilometers through mountains, deserts, and rainforests. Relay runners called chasquis carried messages along these roads, covering as much as 240 kilometers in a single day.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
In this inverted sentence the subject is the singular "road network," and the past-tense context calls for "was."

Zora Neale Hurston's ______ Their Eyes Were Watching God received mixed reviews when it was published in 1937 and later fell out of print for years. Its reputation was revived in the 1970s, after the writer Alice Walker published an essay describing her search for Hurston's unmarked grave in Florida.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
Hurston wrote several novels, so the title is essential information and takes no punctuation; a single comma or dash would also wrongly separate the subject from its verb.

Penguins are birds, but unlike most other birds, they are unable to fly through the air. ______ their wings have evolved into stiff, flattened flippers that make them powerful and efficient swimmers. Emperor penguins can dive deeper than 500 meters to capture fish, squid, and other prey.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
The wings are used for swimming in place of flying, so "Instead" shows the contrast.

Libraries today offer much more than books. Many of them lend laptops and Wi-Fi hotspots to people who do not have internet access at home. ______ some libraries let visitors borrow unusual items such as fishing rods, cake pans, and musical instruments.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
The last sentence adds another example of what libraries offer, so "In addition" fits.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Bessie Coleman was born in Texas in 1892.
• She wanted to become a pilot, but flight schools in the United States would not admit her because she was Black and a woman.
• She learned French and traveled to France to attend a flight school there.
• In 1921, she earned an international pilot's license.
• She was the first African American woman to hold a pilot's license.
The student wants to emphasize how Coleman overcame an obstacle to reach her goal. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

["Although U.S. flight schools refused to admit her, Coleman learned French, trained in France, and earned her pilot's license in 1921.","Bessie Coleman, who was born in Texas in 1892, earned a pilot's license in 1921.","Coleman was born in Texas in 1892 and later became a pilot.","Coleman learned French and traveled to France."]
This choice names the obstacle (being refused by U.S. schools) and how she got past it.

The planet Venus is often called Earth's twin because the two planets are nearly the same size and mass. ______ the surface of Venus could hardly be less like Earth's: temperatures there reach about 465°C, which is hot enough to melt lead. The atmospheric pressure is also more than 90 times greater than on Earth.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
The sentence contrasts Venus's harsh surface with its similarity to Earth, so "However" is logical.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Mangroves are salt-tolerant trees that grow along tropical coastlines.
• Their tangled roots reduce the energy of waves during storms.
• A 2020 study estimated that mangroves prevent more than $65 billion in flood damage worldwide every year.
• Mangrove roots provide shelter for young fish.
• Some mangrove species can filter salt from seawater.
The student wants to emphasize the economic value of mangroves. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

["By reducing the energy of storm waves, mangroves prevent an estimated $65 billion in flood damage worldwide every year.","The roots of mangroves provide shelter for young fish and reduce the energy of waves.","Mangroves are trees that grow along tropical coastlines.","Mangroves are salt-tolerant trees, and some species can filter salt from seawater."]
Only this choice gives a dollar value, directly showing the economic importance of mangroves.

In the early 1900s, electric lights were common in American cities. But running power lines to farms that were spread far apart cost a great deal of money, and power companies saw little profit in it. ______ by 1930, only about one in ten farm homes in the United States had electricity.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
Few farms had power because extending lines was costly, so "As a result" shows the cause-and-effect relationship.

For decades, many astronomers assumed that planets orbiting other stars would be arranged much like those in our own solar system, with giant planets far from their stars. ______ the first planet discovered orbiting a sunlike star, found in 1995, turned out to be a gas giant circling so close to its star that a year there lasts just over four days.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
The discovery contradicted the astronomers' assumption, so a contrasting transition is needed.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Svalbard Global Seed Vault is located on a remote Norwegian island in the Arctic.
• It opened in 2008.
• It preserves duplicate samples of seeds from agricultural gene banks around the world.
• Because the vault is built deep inside a mountain, the seeds remain frozen even if electricity fails.
• In 2015, researchers withdrew seeds from the vault to replace collections damaged during the Syrian civil war.
The student wants to emphasize that the vault's backup seeds have been put to practical use. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

["In 2015, researchers withdrew seeds from the Svalbard vault to replace gene bank collections damaged during the war in Syria.","The Svalbard Global Seed Vault, which opened in 2008, is located on a Norwegian island in the Arctic.","The vault stores backup copies of seeds from gene banks around the world.","Because the vault is built inside a mountain, its seeds stay frozen even if the electricity fails."]
Only this choice describes the backup seeds actually being used to restore lost collections.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Phillis Wheatley and Gwendolyn Brooks were both acclaimed Black American poets.
• Wheatley's collection Poems on Various Subjects, Religious and Moral was published in London in 1773.
• Wheatley often wrote in heroic couplets, a formal style popular in eighteenth-century England.
• Brooks won the 1950 Pulitzer Prize for Poetry for her book Annie Allen.
• Brooks often wrote about everyday life in the Bronzeville neighborhood of Chicago.
The student wants to introduce Brooks's major award to an audience already familiar with Wheatley. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

["Wheatley often wrote in heroic couplets, a formal style popular in eighteenth-century England.","Like Wheatley, whose 1773 collection brought her wide acclaim, Brooks earned great recognition, winning the 1950 Pulitzer Prize for Poetry for Annie Allen.","Phillis Wheatley published Poems on Various Subjects, Religious and Moral in London in 1773.","Gwendolyn Brooks and Phillis Wheatley were both acclaimed Black American poets."]
This choice connects Brooks to the familiar figure of Wheatley and names Brooks's Pulitzer Prize.

Some critics argue that a four-day workweek would reduce output, since employees would simply have fewer hours to finish their tasks. Results from actual trials, however, have challenged this prediction. ______ in a 2022 trial in the United Kingdom, most of the 61 participating companies reported that revenue stayed about the same, and the majority chose to keep the shorter schedule after the trial ended.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
The UK trial is an example of a result that challenged the prediction, so "For instance" fits.

Bioluminescence, the production of light by living things, is common in the deep ocean, where by some estimates three-quarters of animals can make their own light. ______ glowing species on land are relatively rare, limited mostly to fireflies, certain fungi, and a handful of other insects and worms. Scientists suspect the difference reflects the deep sea's darkness, where light is one of the few ways to send signals.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
The rarity of glowing land species contrasts with how common they are in the deep sea.

Early studies of the placebo effect reported that about a third of patients improved after receiving treatments with no active ingredients. Later researchers pointed out that many of these patients might have recovered anyway, since many illnesses fade on their own over time. ______ some apparent placebo effects may reflect the natural course of an illness rather than any response to the fake treatment.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
The final sentence draws a conclusion from the point that patients may have recovered naturally, so "Thus" is logical.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Researchers investigated whether bumblebees could learn to roll a small ball to a target to obtain a sugar reward.
• Some bees learned by observing a trained bee perform the task.
• Other bees observed a hidden magnet moving the ball, with no demonstrator bee present.
• Bees that observed a trained demonstrator learned faster than bees that observed the magnet.
• Several observer bees adopted a more efficient strategy than the one that had been demonstrated.
The student wants to emphasize that the bees did not simply copy what they observed. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

["Bees that watched a trained bee learned the task faster than bees that watched a magnet move the ball.","Some bees learned the task by watching a hidden magnet move the ball to the target.","Researchers tested whether bumblebees could learn to roll a ball to a target for a sugar reward.","Some bees solved the task with a more efficient approach than the one they had been shown, suggesting they were not merely imitating."]
Only this choice shows bees improving on the demonstration rather than copying it.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In a 2019 experiment, researchers turned in more than 17,000 supposedly lost wallets in 355 cities across 40 countries.
• Some wallets contained no money; others contained the equivalent of about $13.45.
• Each wallet included a business card displaying an email address.
• The researchers recorded how frequently each wallet was reported to that address.
• In most countries, wallets containing money were reported more frequently than empty ones.
The student wants to describe the method of the study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

["Researchers wanted to know whether people would return lost wallets.","In most of the 40 countries studied, wallets containing money were reported to their owners more often than empty wallets.","A 2019 study produced surprising results about honesty in countries around the world.","Researchers turned in over 17,000 wallets, some empty and some holding about $13.45, in 355 cities and recorded how often each was reported to an email address on an enclosed business card."]
This choice explains what the researchers did and what they measured, which is the study's method; the first choice is a result.

In 1608, the Dutch spectacle maker Hans Lipperhey asked the government of the Netherlands for a patent on a new device for "seeing things far away as if they were nearby." Officials admired the instrument but declined to grant the patent. ______ they noted, the device was simple to copy, and at least two other craftsmen had already claimed to have built similar instruments.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
The final sentence gives the reason for denying the patent, and "After all" introduces such a justification.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Before 2021, the Norse settlement at L'Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland could be dated only to roughly 1000 CE.
• A burst of radiation from a solar storm in 993 CE left a spike of carbon-14 in tree rings worldwide.
• By finding this spike in wood cut by Norse settlers and counting the rings that grew afterward, researchers determined that the wood was cut in 1021 CE.
• Dendrochronology dates wood by matching patterns of wide and narrow tree rings.
• Radiocarbon dating estimates age by measuring the decay of carbon-14.
The student wants to emphasize how the 2021 study improved on earlier dating of the settlement. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

["A solar storm in 993 CE left a spike of carbon-14 that appears in tree rings around the world.","Whereas the Norse presence at L'Anse aux Meadows had been dated only to roughly 1000 CE, a 2021 study used a carbon-14 spike from 993 CE to show that settlers cut wood there in 1021 CE.","Dendrochronology matches patterns of tree rings, while radiocarbon dating measures the decay of carbon-14.","Researchers studied wood cut by Norse settlers at L'Anse aux Meadows, a site in Newfoundland."]
Only this choice contrasts the earlier rough date with the exact year the 2021 study established.
The historian cautioned that the diary, while vivid, offers only a ____ view of the period, since its author lived in a single village and never traveled.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
One village and no travel means the view is narrow.
The sculptor's style is anything but ____: each of her pieces departs sharply from the last, and no two look as though the same artist made them.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
Pieces that differ sharply are the opposite of uniform.
The physicist's lecture was ____ in the best sense: it distilled decades of dense mathematics into a handful of images that a general audience could grasp.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
Making dense material easy to grasp is clarity, or lucidity.

In 1894, a young lighthouse keeper named Abel Rourke began a journal. He recorded the weather, passing ships, and, increasingly, his loneliness. The journal, discovered in an attic last year, offers historians a rare personal account of coastal life.
Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

["To compare two journals from the same era.","To argue that lighthouse keepers were poorly treated.","To introduce a historical document and explain why it is valuable.","To describe how lighthouses operate."]
The text presents the journal and notes its value to historians.

Many people assume that bees die immediately after stinging. In fact, only honeybees have barbed stingers that lodge in skin; bumblebees and many other species can sting repeatedly. The misconception persists because honeybees are the species people most often encounter.
Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

["It corrects a common belief and then explains why the belief persists.","It presents a hypothesis and then describes an experiment that tests it.","It contrasts two scientific theories and then favors one.","It describes a problem and then proposes a solution."]
The text refutes a misconception and then accounts for it.

Economist Dara Okafor argues that remote work has reshaped small-town economies. Cafes, hardware stores, and childcare centers have reported rising demand since 2020. Critics, however, note that these gains are concentrated in towns within a two-hour drive of a major city. Okafor concedes the point but maintains that even this limited effect is significant.
Which choice best describes the function of the third sentence?

["It introduces a limitation on the claim presented earlier.","It provides a specific example supporting Okafor's claim.","It defines a term used in the previous sentence.","It restates Okafor's central argument in different terms."]
The critics' note qualifies how widely the claimed gains apply.

The kitchen smelled of cardamom and burnt sugar. Nadia stood at the counter, flour to her elbows, listening for her grandmother's footsteps on the stairs. Each creak of the old boards made her heart quicken, though she could not have said whether from fear or hope.
Which choice best describes the overall focus of the text?

["A grandmother's disapproval of her granddaughter's cooking.","A character's detailed recipe for a family dessert.","A character's mixed anticipation as she waits in a familiar setting.","A narrator's regret about leaving a childhood home."]
Nadia feels both fear and hope while waiting.

Archaeologists long interpreted the stone circles of the northern plateau as calendars, aligning each with solstice sunrises. A recent survey, however, found that only four of the thirty-one circles align with any solar event, a proportion no greater than chance would predict. The finding does not rule out ceremonial use, but it undermines the calendar hypothesis as a general explanation.
Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

["To explain how solstices were observed in antiquity.","To defend the calendar hypothesis against criticism.","To propose a new method for surveying ancient sites.","To present new evidence that weakens a long-held interpretation."]
The survey results cast doubt on the calendar hypothesis.

Text 1
Urban planner Lila Moreno argues that cities should replace parking lots with housing, since doing so would ease the housing shortage.

Text 2
Transportation analyst Greg Hale cautions that removing parking without improving public transit could strand residents who depend on cars.
Based on the texts, how would Hale most likely respond to Moreno's argument?

["By arguing that parking lots are more valuable than housing in every case.","By proposing that cities build more parking garages instead.","By denying that a housing shortage exists in cities.","By agreeing that parking could be replaced but insisting that transit improvements accompany the change."]
Hale warns against removing parking without better transit, not against the idea itself.

Text 1
Some linguists claim that children acquire grammar mainly through an innate capacity, noting that all children, regardless of upbringing, master complex rules by age five.

Text 2
Linguist Pei Chen found that children exposed to richer conversation at home mastered certain constructions months earlier than peers with less exposure, suggesting that input matters more than the Text 1 view allows.
Which choice best describes how Text 2 relates to Text 1?

["It applies the view described in Text 1 to a different language.","It offers evidence that complicates the view described in Text 1.","It restates the view described in Text 1 with additional examples.","It explains the biological origin of the capacity described in Text 1."]
Chen's findings suggest input plays a larger role than the innate-capacity view admits.

Few visitors to the gallery notice the small brass plaque beside Ito's painting. Yet the plaque tells the story of its rescue: in 1962, a flood submerged the storage vault, and conservators spent three years restoring the canvas. The painting, in other words, survives not only because of Ito's skill but also because of the patience of those who saved it.
Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

["To explain the techniques Ito used to paint the canvas.","To criticize the gallery for hiding the plaque.","To describe the causes of the 1962 flood.","To suggest that the painting's survival reflects the work of conservators as well as its creator."]
The final sentence credits both the artist and the conservators.

Tomas planted tomato seeds in early April. By late May, the seedlings were tall enough to move outside, and by August the plants were heavy with fruit. Tomas gave most of the tomatoes to his neighbors.
According to the text, what did Tomas do with most of the tomatoes?
["He sold them at a market.","He canned them for winter.","He saved their seeds.","He gave them to his neighbors."]
The final sentence states he gave most to neighbors.

Octopuses are known for their intelligence. In laboratory tests, they have opened jars, solved mazes, and even escaped from sealed tanks. Researchers say these abilities suggest that complex problem solving evolved in more than one branch of the animal kingdom.
Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

["Octopuses display problem-solving abilities that interest researchers.","Jars are commonly found in ocean habitats.","Octopuses are difficult to keep in laboratory tanks.","Mazes are the best way to test animal intelligence."]
The text centers on octopus intelligence and its significance.
When the town library extended its hours in March, the number of visitors per week rose from about 400 to about 650. The library director noted that most of the new visitors arrived after 6 p.m.
Which choice is most strongly supported by the text?

["Most visitors prefer the library to other town services.","The number of visitors will keep rising every month.","The extended hours made the library accessible to some people who could not previously visit.","The library's collection expanded in March."]
New evening visitors suggest later hours reached people who could not come earlier.
Fourth-grade teacher Ms. Adeyemi asks students to keep a weather log for one month. Each day, they record the temperature, cloud cover, and wind direction, and at month's end they graph the results.
According to the text, what do students do at the end of the month?
["They graph the results of their observations.","They compare their logs with a meteorologist's.","They predict the next month's weather.","They present their logs to the principal."]
The text says they graph the results at month's end.

Tardigrades survive extreme conditions by entering a dried-out state in which their metabolism nearly stops. In 2017, researchers identified a protein unique to tardigrades that appears to shield their DNA from radiation damage. When that protein was introduced into human cells in the lab, the cells showed less damage after exposure to X-rays.
Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

["Tardigrades are the only animals that can survive without water.","Human cells are naturally more resistant to X-rays than tardigrade cells.","Researchers have developed a way for humans to survive extreme conditions.","A protein found in tardigrades may protect DNA, and it reduced radiation damage even in human cells grown in a lab."]
The text describes the protein and its protective effect in human cells.

Historian Priya Anand notes that the village's records show no births between 1846 and 1849, while burial entries doubled. She adds that the records resume normal patterns in 1850, with a sharp rise in baptisms.
Which choice is most strongly supported by the text?

["The village's record keeper retired in 1850.","Burial entries rose because the village grew larger.","The village likely experienced a crisis that affected its population in the late 1840s.","Baptisms were illegal before 1850."]
No births, doubled burials, and a later rebound suggest a population crisis.

Ruth Calloway's novel follows a fishing family. Early on, the narrator calls the harbor "a cradle rocking the town to sleep." Near the end, the narrator calls the same water "a hungry mouth waiting beyond the rocks." The family's boat, the Marigold, appears in nearly every chapter.
A student claims that Calloway portrays the sea ambivalently. Which choice best supports the student's claim?

["The narrator describes the harbor only once.","The narrator calls the harbor a cradle early in the novel and a hungry mouth near the end.","The novel follows a fishing family.","The Marigold appears in nearly every chapter."]
Contrasting images of the same water show conflicting attitudes.

Ecologist Hana Sato hypothesizes that urban birds sing at higher pitches because low-pitched songs are masked by traffic noise. To test this, she recorded great tits in quiet forests and in noisy city parks.
Which finding, if true, would most directly support Sato's hypothesis?

["Great tits in city parks sang at a higher average pitch than great tits in forests.","Great tits in both settings sang at the same pitch.","Great tits in forests sang more often than those in city parks.","Great tits in city parks were larger than those in forests."]
A higher pitch in noisy places matches the hypothesis.
A school surveyed 200 students about how they travel to class. Of those students, 80 walked, 60 rode the bus, 40 were driven by family, and 20 biked.
Which choice most accurately describes data from the survey?

["Biking was used by 20 percent of students.","Riding the bus was the most common method, used by 40 percent of students.","Being driven by family was used by half of students.","Walking was the most common method, used by 40 percent of students."]
80 of 200 is 40 percent, the largest group.
A librarian recorded the books checked out in one week: fiction, 310; nonfiction, 150; poetry, 40; graphic novels, 100. She wants to show that fiction made up more than half of all checkouts.
Which choice most effectively uses the data to support her claim?

["Poetry accounted for the fewest checkouts, at 40.","Fiction accounted for 310 of the 600 books checked out, which is more than half.","Nonfiction and graphic novels together accounted for 250 checkouts.","Fiction accounted for 310 checkouts, more than any other category."]
310 of 600 exceeds 50 percent, directly supporting the claim.

Elena had practiced the cello piece for weeks, but when she stepped onto the stage, the audience's silence made her hands tremble. She closed her eyes, remembered her teacher's advice to breathe slowly, and began to play.
What does Elena do to steady herself?
["She asks the audience for quiet.","She looks for her teacher in the front row.","She switches to a simpler piece.","She closes her eyes and recalls her teacher's advice about breathing."]
The text says she closed her eyes and remembered the breathing advice.

Scholars once attributed the unsigned portrait to the workshop of a famous master, citing its confident brushwork. But infrared imaging has revealed underdrawings that differ markedly from the master's documented habits, and the pigments include a blue unavailable in the region until a generation after his death.
Which choice is most strongly supported by the text?

["The master's brushwork was inconsistent throughout his career.","The portrait was probably not produced in the master's workshop during his lifetime.","The portrait was painted by someone deliberately imitating the master.","Infrared imaging cannot be used on portraits."]
Differing underdrawings and an anachronistic pigment argue against the attribution.

Urban beekeeping has grown quickly, but ecologists warn that it can backfire. Honeybees compete with native pollinators for limited flowers, and in cities with few green spaces, the added competition may reduce native bee populations. The researchers recommend planting more flowers before adding hives.
Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

["Cities should ban beekeeping entirely.","Native bees prefer cities to rural areas.","Urban beekeeping may harm native pollinators unless enough flowering plants are available.","Honeybees are less effective pollinators than native bees."]
The text warns of competition and recommends adding flowers first.
Every morning, the baker at Corner Loaf arrives at 4 a.m. By 6 a.m., a line of customers is already waiting outside the door.
Which choice is most strongly supported by the text?
["The customers bake their own bread.","Corner Loaf opens at 4 a.m.","Corner Loaf's bread is popular with customers.","The baker dislikes early mornings."]
An early line of customers suggests the bread is popular.

Volcanologist Sam Ortiz measures gas emissions at the crater's rim before and after each eruption. Before the 2019 eruption, sulfur dioxide levels climbed for two weeks. Ortiz suggests that tracking such increases could help officials issue earlier warnings.
Which choice best states Ortiz's suggestion?

["Craters should be measured only after eruptions.","Sulfur dioxide is the only gas worth measuring.","Eruptions can be prevented by reducing gas emissions.","Rising sulfur dioxide levels may serve as an early warning of eruptions."]
The final sentence proposes using gas increases for earlier warnings.

Economists often treat price as the main signal of a good's value, yet studies of secondhand markets suggest that provenance also shapes willingness to pay. In one experiment, identical mugs sold for nearly twice as much when buyers were told they had belonged to a celebrated poet. The results imply that value is partly a story buyers tell themselves.
Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

["Economists disagree about how to measure prices.","Buyers' valuation of goods can depend on narratives about an item as well as its price.","Secondhand markets are more efficient than new-goods markets.","Mugs that belonged to poets are more durable than other mugs."]
The experiment shows a story about the item changing what buyers will pay.
At a science fair, 5 projects were in botany, 8 in chemistry, 4 in physics, and 3 in astronomy. Judges awarded ribbons to 2 botany, 4 chemistry, 1 physics, and 1 astronomy projects.
Which category had the highest proportion of its projects awarded ribbons?
Chemistry 4/8 is 50 percent, higher than botany 40, astronomy about 33, and physics 25.

When Ansel returned to the village after thirty years, he found the mill silent and the millpond choked with reeds. He walked its length slowly, touching the splintered railing as though it might answer him.
Which choice best describes Ansel's reaction?

["He is eager to restart the mill himself.","He is irritated that the village ignored his return.","He is indifferent to the changes.","He is moved by the decline of a place that once mattered to him."]

Leo and his grandfather had a special plan. They were going to build a wooden birdhouse together before spring arrived.

Grandpa carefully laid out the boards, a box of nails, and a small hammer on the workbench. "First we measure, then we cut, and then we build," he explained.

But Leo did not want to measure anything, because he wanted to start building right away. He grabbed two boards and began to hammer as fast as he could. The nails went in crooked, the roof slid off to one side, and the little door was too big.

Leo frowned at his work. "It looks like it is about to fall down," he said.

Grandpa smiled. "Lots of good things start out a little crooked," he said. "Shall we try again, slowly this time?"

So they tried again, and this time Leo held the ruler steady while Grandpa marked the wood with a pencil. They cut each board with care, and Leo tapped every nail in straight. The work took the whole afternoon.

When they were finished, the new birdhouse stood tall and even. They hung it on the maple tree beside the kitchen window.

Leo decided to keep the crooked birdhouse too, so he set it on a low branch just for fun.

A week later, Leo ran excitedly to find Grandpa. "Look!" he cried. A small brown wren was carrying twigs into the crooked birdhouse. Grandpa laughed and said, "I guess that bird likes your first try best."

["The boards were too wet to use.","The hammer was too heavy for him.","He rushed and did not measure first.","Grandpa gave him the wrong nails."]
Leo "did not want to measure anything, because he wanted to start building right away," so the nails went in crooked.

Rosa had been planning her lemonade stand for a whole week. She painted a sign with bright yellow letters, and she squeezed a big pitcher of lemons with her dad. Saturday was going to be perfect.

But on Saturday morning, Rosa woke up to the sound of rain tapping on her window. The sky was gray, and the air outside felt cold. Rosa pressed her nose against the glass and sighed.

"Nobody wants cold lemonade on a gloomy day like this," she said.

Her dad nodded slowly. "You may be right," he said. "So what do people want on a cold, rainy day?"

Rosa thought about it carefully. She remembered how she felt whenever she came inside after playing in the rain. Then she smiled. "They want something warm!" she said.

Together they made a big pot of hot cocoa. Rosa turned her sign over, and on the back she wrote HOT COCOA in big brown letters. She set up her table under the porch roof, where it would stay dry.

Soon a mail carrier stopped by, shaking the water off her hat. Then came a man walking his dog, and after him two children in rain boots. Each visitor held a warm cup in their cold hands and smiled.

By noon, the pot was completely empty. Rosa counted her coins and grinned. "Maybe rainy days are not so bad after all," she said.

On Saturday morning Rosa "woke up to the sound of rain" and the air was cold, so she thinks no one will want lemonade.

Sea otters live in the chilly ocean waters along the coast of the North Pacific. Most sea animals have a thick layer of fat to keep them warm, but sea otters do not. Instead, they have the thickest fur of any animal on Earth. A patch of otter fur the size of a stamp has more hairs than a person has on a whole head! The fur traps tiny bubbles of air, and the air keeps the otter's skin warm and dry.

To keep their fur working well, sea otters spend hours each day cleaning it. They rub, comb, and fluff it with their paws, because a dirty coat would let in the cold water.

Sea otters must eat a lot of food to stay warm. They dive to the sea floor to find clams, crabs, and sea urchins. Some otters bring up a flat rock, too. They float on their backs and rest the rock on their bellies. Then they bang the shells against the rock until the shells crack open. Sea otters are one of the few animals that use tools.

When it is time to sleep, a sea otter does not want to drift away. So it wraps itself in long strands of kelp, a kind of seaweed that grows up from the ocean floor. The kelp works like an anchor and keeps the otter in place while it naps on the waves.

["how sea otters stay warm, eat, and rest in the ocean","why sea otters are the best swimmers in the sea","why most sea animals have a thick layer of fat","how kelp grows up from the ocean floor"]
Each paragraph describes a way otters live in the cold ocean: their fur, cleaning, finding food with tools, and sleeping in kelp.

Plants cannot walk, but their seeds can still go on long journeys. A seed that lands right under its parent plant may not grow well, because the big plant blocks the sunlight and drinks up most of the water. So plants have many clever ways to send their seeds far away.

Some seeds ride the wind. A dandelion seed has a puff of soft hairs, like a tiny umbrella, and when the wind blows, the seed floats away. Maple seeds have flat wings that spin like little helicopters as they fall.

Other seeds hitch a ride on animals. Burdock seeds are covered in small hooks that stick to the fur of a passing dog or deer. Later, the seeds fall off in a new place. Birds help too. They eat berries, and the seeds inside drop to the ground far away.

Some seeds travel by water. A coconut is a very large seed with a hard shell that keeps water out. It can float on the ocean for weeks and finally land on a faraway beach.

Wind, animals, and water all help plants spread out to new places. That way, each new plant can find its own space to grow.
